The Indikatoroversigt provides a structured framework of 11 quality indicators designed to monitor and evaluate the clinical care of patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1]. These metrics, which align with the oversight objectives of the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]], are categorized into process indicators (Proces) that track clinical actions, and outcome indicators (Resultat) that measure patient health events [^src1].

An analysis of the established targets (Standard) reveals distinct priorities in clinical expectations. The leaders among process indicators—those with the strictest compliance thresholds—are Indikator 3 (TSH measurement around the time of diagnosis) and Indikator 4b (annual S-creatinine measurement for patients on Direct Oral Anticoagulants), both requiring a ≥ 95% compliance rate [^src1]. The trailer among the process metrics is Indikator 8, which tracks the provision of a structured education program to newly diagnosed patients within their first year, carrying a significantly lower target of ≥ 50% [^src1]. For the outcome indicators, the strictest threshold is applied to the incidence of intracranial bleeding (Indikator 6) at ≤ 0.6%, while the incidence of stroke (Indikator 5) allows a slightly higher rate of ≤ 0.8% [^src1]. 

A notable outlier in this dataset is Indikator 7, which monitors the incidence of major bleeding among prevalent patients; it is the only indicator lacking a defined numerical standard or target (—) [^src1]. Additionally, while the framework sets clear longitudinal goals for anticoagulation treatment retention at one, two, and five years post-index date (all ≥ 90%), this specific document only outlines the predefined standards rather than the actual clinical results [^src1]. Consequently, it is impossible to determine which targets were met or missed based on this data alone [^src1]. Furthermore, because this comparison relies on a single dated section, no historical trends regarding the improvement or decline of these metrics over time can be established [^src1].
